ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, beneficial clients, and transaction parties against the French national asset-freeze registry, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list for all USD-denominated or US-correspondent-bank transfers. PEP status is assessed in accordance with Article L561-2(4) of the French Monetary and Financial Code and FATF Recommendations 12, 22, and 25. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, high-risk third-country involvement, complex ownership structures, or inconsistent source-of-funds information. Automated sanctions/UBO screening must be completed before onboarding and refreshed continuously thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name search and published registration data via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be expressed in any language but must be registered in Latin alphabetic characters in the RNE and all RCS filings. If the intended name contains nonscript characters, a Latin-alphabet transliteration must be filed with the original form shown in parentheses. The name must not mislead as to legal form, activity, or public authority, and must be followed by the mandatory suffix 'Société par actions simplifiée' or 'SAS'. French language is obligatory only for instruments submitted to French registries, employment documents, invoices, and commercial documents required under French law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RNE/INPI or the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant may within 15 days of the rejection notice submit a written request for reconsideration directly to the Registry Officer (greffier) via the guichet unique. Where refusal is based on a ministry's opposition to a sensitive token, the applicant may file a hierarchical administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) with the Minister of Economy and Finance within two months, and thereafter a challenge before the Conseil d'État. If the rejection is grounded on prior third-party trademark rights, the applicant may file an opposition or seek cancellation proceedings before the Cour de justice de l'Union européenne or the French courts; a civil summary petition to the President of the Commercial Court under Articles 851 et seq. of the French Code of Civil Procedure is available for registry refusals. All appeals must be filed within the applicable statutory limitation period, typically 30 days from notification of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or professional domiciliation company is permitted for an SAS in this regulatory-consulting industry under Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, provided the domiciliary is an authorized société de domiciliation and corporate records are accessible at that address. However, if the entity intends to act as an EU Authorized Representative under the EU Medical Device Regulation, or as a sponsor or importer of record, a physical French office with actual operational capability is strongly recommended and may be expected by notified bodies and ANSM.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5%) annualized probability of unannounced physical inspection for a pure regulatory-consulting entity not storing devices or controlled substances. Probability rises to ~15-20% if the company assumes MDR Article 31 Authorized Representative obligations, holds a French ANSM establishment authorization, or carries ISO 13485 certification entitling unannounced notified-body audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VIII: Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-30 and R. 227-1 to R. 227-11 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general company provisions of the Civil Code Articles 1832 to 1844-17; Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS registration executed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de Constitution (online dynamic dossier of the Guichet Unique, equivalent to Cerfa Form No. 15702) submitted with the signed Statuts (Articles of Association).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for an SAS (may be set as low as EUR 1); however, where cash capital is stated, at least 50% of the subscribed cash capital must be paid up at incorporation and the balance within five years. Funds must be deposited with a French licensed bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and the attestation de dépôt de fonds must accompany the filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF ______ SAS. The Shareholder, having reviewed the draft Statuts, resolves: 1. Share Subscription — the subscription of ___ shares with par value of €___ each, aggregating €___ in share capital, is accepted and ratified. 2. Registered Office — the Company’s registered office is fixed at ___ for the duration of the Articles. 3. Officers — ___ is appointed Président, with full powers granted by the Articles; ___ is appointed Directeur Général, if applicable. 4. Ratification — all instruments and publications completed for incorporation are ratified, including the capital deposit certificate. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Statuts and Internal Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders under private seal (sous seing privé); notarization required only for in-kind contributions of real property or gratuitous transfers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French stating corporate name, legal form SAS, registered office, corporate object, share capital, share distribution, powers of the President, admission and transfer rules, and collective decision processes. Verify name availability and SIREN number via the INPI/Infogreffe database. Execute the First Board Resolution approving share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. If in-kind contributions are made, have the Commissaire aux apports issue a valuation report.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and President
Proof of occupation/domiciliation of the registered office
Commissaire aux apports report (if in-kind contributions)
Declaration of beneficial ownership (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Statuts are rejected or queried, pass a supplementary general assembly resolution correcting the articles and resubmit the rectified version through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the cash portion of the subscribed capital. Obtain from the financial institution the attestation de dépôt de fonds (certificate of deposit) referencing the depositor, beneficiary company, and amount. This certificate is a mandatory annex to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Order to open the temporary account
Statuts draft confirming the capital amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the attestation pending further KYC documentation, provide the requested corporate and identity documents; any discrepancy in the deposited amount must be corrected by a shareholder’s rectification deposit before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in an Authorized Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d’Annonces Légales (JAL) of the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the legal notice of incorporation in a JAL authorized in the department of the registered office. The notice must state the corporate name, legal form, share capital, address of the registered office, corporate object, and the identity of the President. The publication date must be within one month before filing. Obtain the publisher’s certificat de parution.
required_dossiers: Identification data of the company and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL publication certificate contains errors, request immediate rectification and re-publication; a corrected certificate must be uploaded to the Guichet Unique before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation Application on the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI — Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, online portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the dynamic online incorporation form, attaching the signed Statuts, bank deposit certificate, JAL publication certificate, proof of occupation of the registered office, appointment instruments, and the declaration of beneficial ownership. Pay the official state filing fee by bank card. Submit the digital dossier; the INPI performs completeness checks and routes the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, tax authorities, and URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI issues a request for additional documents (demande de pièces complémentaires), respond through the secure messaging portal within fifteen days; failure to respond causes lapse of the application. Correct and resubmit the incomplete items promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following INPI transmission, the Greffe verifies the legal regularity of the dossier and registers the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, allocating the SIREN, SIRET, and RCS number. Legal personality is acquired only upon registration. Download the electronic Kbis extract from Infogreffe and verify all corporate details for accuracy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration for formal irregularity, adopt a corrective resolution or amend the Statuts and refile through the Guichet Unique; the registration is not subject to substantive licensing review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, DREETS (labor inspection), and the corporate bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the definitive corporate bank account in the company’s name and transfer funds from the temporary capital account. Register with URSSAF for social security obligations and obtain the permanent company identifiers. Maintain statutory books including the share register (registre des titres de capital) and decisions register under Article L. 227-9. Prepare the employee register and occupational health documentation prior to hiring staff.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or the bank raises compliance objections, rectify the declarations through the respective secure portals and provide the requested Kbis or supporting documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — office-based MedTech regulatory consulting under NAF 7490B is a tertiary service activity and is not subject to industrial installation licensing (no ICPE regime).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no licence d’exploitation is required for this non-statutory consulting activity; ordinary commercial registration evidenced by the Kbis suffices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction Régionale de l’Environnement, de l’Aménagement et du Logement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative office use does not fall within the ICPE nomenclature (Environmental Code Articles L. 511-1 and R. 512-1) and no EIA is required under R. 122-2 for a class 7490 consulting entity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC/HAP emissions arise from the activity. Office sanitary effluents must comply with the municipal sewer discharge bylaws; any negligible electronic or IT waste must be routed through channeled EPR collection schemes in accordance with the Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require fire safety compliance as a 5th-category ERP under Articles R. 123-1 et seq. of the Code de la Construction et de l’Habitation, with a fire safety certificate issued by the Commission de Sécurité; structural load inspection for standard office floor loading by the building owner; and occupational health and evacuation compliance under Articles L. 4121-1, L. 4222-1 and R. 4222-1 et seq. of the Code du Travail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating through the national portal impots.gouv.fr and the decentralized Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) assigned to the SAS registered office; non-resident and cross-border matters are handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) and the Direction des Résidents à l'Étranger et des Services Généraux (DRESG).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SAS via the Guichet des Formalités Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) to receive SIREN/SIRET from INSEE; 2) the SIRET is the domestic tax account identifier and the SIREN forms the base of the EU VAT number (FR + 2-digit control key + SIREN), automatically allocated by the SIE upon registration (Article 286 CGI); 3) for a non-established foreign entity operating with or without a permanent establishment in France, registration for VAT is made with the SIEE using CERFA Form No. 14080 (Demande d'immatriculation), naming a fiscal representative with joint and several liability (Article 289 A CGI) when the entity is established outside the EU; 4) corporate income tax registration is completed via Form No. 1000 (Extrait d'immatriculation) filed within 30 days of creating a French permanent establishment; 5) a foreign SAS shareholder is not required to obtain a French tax ID for purely passive investment, but the SAS must file the annual beneficial ownership declaration (RBE) under Article 1649 C CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: An SAS is by default fully subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under Article 206-1 CGI on its worldwide profits, with a reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of taxable income (for taxpayers with turnover ≤ €10 million) and the standard 25% rate above; foreign branch income is exempt under the French territoriality principle (Article 209 CGI); Tax-Exempt Zone: no general tax-free zone applies to a commercial SAS registered in metropolitan France, although overseas-department specific regimes (e.g., LODEOM) exist but are not available to a mainland-registered consulting entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Pass-through election under Article 239 bis AA CGI: a qualifying small SAS (created by natural persons, 50-100% of capital held by individuals who are also manager-directors, turnover ≤ €10 million, exercising a commercial/liberal activity) may elect to be taxed as a conduit under Impôt sur le Revenu (IR) for up to 5 fiscal years, with irrevocable waiver permitted; 2) Young Innovative Company (JEI) regime under Article 44 sexies CGI for SAS with qualifying R&D expenditure ≥ 15%, giving a 3-year full corporate income tax exemption; 3) VAT franchise en base de TVA exemption under Article 293 B CGI is automatic below the thresholds but the SAS may positively elect to waive it; 4) Corporate income tax group consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI requires ≥ 95% direct/indirect ownership and is effective for at least 5 tax years; 5) No US-style check-the-box exists in France; hybrid entity classification is denied and subject to OECD BEPS Action 2 / Articles 205-212 quinquies CGI anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) under Articles 256 to 289 E CGI implementing Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €36,800 annual turnover (dominant services and liberal professions, 2024-2025 threshold) and €91,900 (dominant supply of goods) for the franchise en base de TVA exemption under Article 293 B CGI; the following-year threshold is exceeded at €39,100 / €101,000 respectively; a newly created SAS must register from its first taxable transaction if it does not qualify for the franchise, whereas a non-established foreign entity supplying taxable services in France is automatically in scope without any minimum threshold and must use reverse-charge, OSS, or direct registration mechanisms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing under Ordonnance n° 2022-1290, phased from 1 September 2026 (all enterprises must receive; large and mid-size enterprises must issue) and 1 September 2027 (SMEs/micro-enterprises must issue); structured PDF/A3-Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats must be transmitted through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDP) with mandatory semantic controls; e-reporting of B2C transaction and payment data is transmitted to the DGFiP by the 10th day of the month following the transaction; France does not operate an Italian-style real-time fiscal stamping or per-invoice authorization clearance, but the PPF/PDP API architecture performs real-time schema validation, blockchain-grade traceability, and cross-referencing with VIES, enabling immediate audit flags on VAT ID mismatches and zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU are zero-rated (0% TVA) under Articles 262-I-1 and 262-I-2 CGI if the physical export is completed and evidenced within a 90-day period from the tax becoming chargeable; for the core FDA 510(k) / CE Mark regulatory consulting services, French VAT is displaced by the place-of-supply rule in Article 259-1 CGI when the client is established outside France (B2B intra-EU supplies to taxable persons follow reverse-charge under Article 259 A CGI, while B2B supplies to non-EU clients are territorially excluded under Article 259 B CGI and bear no French VAT); eligibility is conditioned on obtaining and preserving the client's EU VAT number (VIES validated) or, for non-EU clients, a certification of establishment outside the EU, the contract, and correspondence evidencing the supply of consultancy and the absence of any French establishment of the recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU) filed in the DELTA-X electronic system for physical goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing departure from EU territory within 90 days
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and Incoterms clause demonstrating transfer of risk and possession
Client EU VAT registration listing (VIES printout) or non-EU establishment certificate (e.g., overseas company registry excerpt)
Bank wire confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate proving settlement from the non-EU or cross-border client
Supporting performance dossier for the consulting engagement (scope of work, FDA/CE submission tracking, correspondence) to substantiate the genuineness of the offshore service supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation rule; the 180-day parameter serves as the prudent evidentiary benchmark because the DGFiP, under Articles L. 13 AA and L. 13 B LPF, presumes the non-existence of an export operation where payment is not received within reasonable commercial terms and may reclassify the entire turnover as domestic taxable supplies at 20% TVA; penalties then apply cumulatively: intérêts de retard at 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI), a 40% bad-faith penalty (Article 1729 CGI) or 80% penalty for organised fraud (Article 1730 CGI), a 5% late-filing penalty (Article 1731 bis CGI), and a 100% clawback of improperly zero-rated VAT under Article 1788 A CGI for missing intra-EU removals; criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI (€500,000 fine / 5 years' imprisonment, increased to €3 million / 7 years when committed by an organised gang) may be charged, and the SAS president may be held personally and jointly liable under Article L. 267 LPF where fraudulent manoeuvres rendered the corporate collection impossible.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, as the French central bank within the Eurosystem; the European Central Bank is responsible for euro monetary policy and relevant Eurosystem payment-system oversight. The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution supervises French credit institutions and certain payment institutions, while the Autorité des marchés financiers supervises investment services and financial markets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions within the European Union framework. France generally has no exchange-control approval requirement for foreign ownership, capital contributions, intercompany loans, dividend payments, service fees, royalty payments, or repatriation of lawful profits. Transactions remain subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, and financial-reporting rules. French banks may require evidence of the transaction purpose, source of funds, beneficial ownership, tax residence, contractual basis, and corporate approvals before execution. Dividend distributions by an SAS require distributable profits or reserves, approved financial statements, and applicable withholding-tax analysis. French domestic dividend withholding is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions, statutory exemptions, and anti-abuse requirements. Interest, royalties, and service payments require separate withholding-tax, treaty, VAT, transfer-pricing, and beneficial-ownership analysis. Non-EU investment-screening, sanctions, and foreign-subsidy rules may apply to transactions involving sensitive activities or restricted counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no general statutory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring export receipts to be converted into euros or deposited with a French bank. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through other lawful EU or international banking channels. The company must retain commercial, customs, invoice, transport, and settlement records and comply with applicable accounting, VAT, Intrastat, customs, statistical, tax, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more entering or leaving the European Union must be declared to customs, and intra-EU cash transport is subject to applicable French reporting rules. Banks may impose contractual transaction-monitoring, documentary, and reporting requirements even though no currency-surrender obligation exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS share-capital formation; Operational Current Account; EUR and permitted foreign-currency accounts; SEPA and SWIFT transaction services
Capital Deposit Account for SAS share-capital formation; Operational Current Account; EUR and foreign-currency accounts; trade-finance, SEPA, TARGET and SWIFT services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account; Capital Deposit Account through an appropriate Crédit Agricole group entity; foreign-currency, cash-management and trade-finance services
Capital Deposit Account and Operational Corporate Account through the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity; SEPA, foreign-currency and payment services
Operational Corporate Account; availability of capital-deposit and international-cash-management products must be confirmed for the proposed SAS profile

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment operations and low to medium for full treasury banking. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA transfers, card acquiring, foreign-exchange conversion, and certain cross-border services under passporting or local authorisation. An EMI payment account is not a bank deposit, normally does not provide deposit insurance, and may not be suitable for statutory capital deposits, overdrafts, complex trade finance, custody of restricted funds, or high-value treasury concentration. Offshore non-EU digital EMIs cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to French customers merely by operating online; they require an applicable EU authorisation, passport, French establishment or lawful cross-border basis, and compliance with French and EU AML, sanctions, safeguarding, outsourcing, data-protection, and consumer rules. The company should maintain a regulated French or EU bank as the primary account and use an EMI only as a documented secondary rail after confirming safeguarding, settlement-bank exposure, account-closure rights, geographic coverage, and permitted business activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal rule that all SAS directors must appear physically to open a bank account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can verify identity, beneficial ownership, authority, source of funds, registered office, business purpose, and expected activity using an acceptable electronic-identification process. Banks may nevertheless require a video interview, certified identity documents, a French address, a local signatory, an in-person appointment, or notarised and apostilled documents, particularly for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership chains, foreign funding, high-risk jurisdictions, or unexplained international flows. A capital-deposit account for incorporation is subject to each bank's procedures and normally requires corporate formation documents, draft articles, shareholder information, and proof of the capital subscription.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with no established French operating footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract or draft Kbis-equivalent formation file; signed articles of association; shareholder register and ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; tax-residence certificates; board or shareholder appointment resolutions; lease, domiciliation agreement, website, commercial pipeline, and French operating plan; explanation of why France is the contracting and banking location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque, layered, nominee, trust, or corporate ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete certified corporate registry extracts for every entity; constitutional documents; ownership and control chart; beneficial-owner declarations; trust or foundation instruments where relevant; director registers; source-of-wealth statements; independent corporate-services-provider confirmation; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a shareholder, group company, or third party whose relationship to the SAS is unclear
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement, shareholder resolution, capital table, bank statements evidencing source of funds, audited or management financial statements of the funder, loan agreement if debt-funded, intercompany agreement, tax-residence evidence, transfer-pricing support, payment instruction identifying the exact purpose, and confirmation that the remitter is not acting for an undisclosed third party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity described as regulatory consulting with potential medical-device, FDA, sanctions, dual-use, or restricted-country exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service catalogue; client and geography policy; statement that the SAS does not manufacture, distribute, import, export, or place medical devices on the market unless separately authorised; sample engagement letters; compliance manual; sanctions and export-control screening procedure; beneficial-owner screening; confirmation of applicable professional, data-protection, and confidentiality controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected international turnover inconsistent with a small or newly incorporated SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year budget; signed or draft customer contracts; invoices and purchase orders; expected monthly payment matrix by country, currency, counterparty type, and purpose; staffing and premises plan; tax and accounting model; explanation of payment intermediaries; treasury policy and transaction-approval matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent foreign-currency conversions, payments to unrelated third parties, or pass-through receipts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written funds-flow map; transaction-purpose codes; underlying contracts and invoices; reconciliation policy; segregation of client funds from company funds; prohibition on unlicensed money transmission; counterparty due-diligence files; annual review controls; documented rationale for each currency and payment corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual assets, privacy-enhancing payment methods, cash-intensive settlements, or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved prohibition or control policy; wallet and exchange records if applicable; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; sanctions screening; enhanced due diligence; legal opinion on regulated status; evidence that all settlement occurs through regulated institutions and that no third-party payment service is being provided without authorisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent company, tax, address, director, or beneficial-owner information across documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extracts; corrected corporate records; explanatory chronology; notarised translations where required; tax identification evidence; updated beneficial-owner filing; director powers and signing authorities; written confirmation from the registered-office provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person status, sanctions match, or high-risk-country nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution analysis distinguishing false positives; official identity documents; PEP declaration; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds package; enhanced due-diligence report; legal and compliance approval; sanctions licence or competent-authority analysis where relevant; transaction restrictions and enhanced monitoring plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a French or EU regulated bank to the SAS capital-deposit account before incorporation or to the operational account after incorporation. The remitter should be the subscribing shareholder or clearly documented group funding entity, not an unexplained third party. Use the payment narrative and bank purpose field to identify 'share capital subscription', 'shareholder contribution', 'shareholder loan', or 'intercompany loan', as applicable. Provide the subscription agreement, shareholder resolution, draft or executed articles, capital table, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, and loan documentation where relevant. After incorporation, obtain the certificate of deposit and release the funds to the SAS operating account. For subsequent funding, reconcile the incoming payment to the accounting entry and determine whether it is equity, a premium contribution, a current-account advance, or debt. Apply arm's-length interest and transfer-pricing documentation to related-party loans. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfers for non-SEPA currencies or corridors. Screen all parties, banks, jurisdictions, and payment narratives against applicable EU and French sanctions and retain transfer records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer, where available and appropriate, for euro supplier and professional-service payments within SEPA. Use SWIFT payment messaging, ordinarily MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent such as pacs.008 as implemented by the relevant banks, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. For documentary trade, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, with documents aligned to the sales contract, invoice, transport document, insurance evidence, customs requirements, and applicable Incoterms. Use documentary collections only where the counterparty and country risk are acceptable. For ordinary regulatory-consulting services, bank transfer against invoice is generally preferable to a commercial LC because there may be no shipment or title documents. Require dual approval, beneficiary verification, invoice-to-contract matching, segregation of duties, sanctions screening, duplicate-payment detection, and reconciliation. Do not use personal accounts, undisclosed third-party payers, informal netting, or payment structures that could constitute unlicensed money transmission.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or authorised investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or committed receivables, payables, or funding exposures and supported by a treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, counterparty, documentation, and settlement method are legally available; assess MiFID II classification, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation requirements, collateral terms, and counterparty eligibility.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps with regulated counterparties for identified funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR requirements, valuation, collateral, accounting, and board-authorised limits.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion through regulated banks or authorised payment providers.

FX options or collars only where commercially justified, properly documented, approved under the treasury policy, and assessed for MiFID II classification, product-governance, valuation, accounting, and potential leveraged-loss risks.

The SAS should not speculate in currencies, provide FX services to third parties, or enter derivatives without an identifiable underlying exposure and appropriate counterparty, legal, accounting, collateral, and internal-control review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 30 each year for the prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of turnover per month of delay, possible administrative sanctions or company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements with the Commercial Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g. June 30 for December 31 fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, potential dissolution proceedings for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after fiscal year end or as extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, interest on unpaid tax, and possible tax audits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or total assets exceed €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration and update of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Bénéficiaires Effectifs) to the tax authorities, required upon changes or annually reviewed

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,000-3,000 USD (depending on company size and audit requirements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €38,120 of taxable profit for companies with turnover < €10 million; research tax credit (CIR) for qualified R&D activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2065-A to 2065-SD) filed via the French tax authority's online portal (impots.gouv.fr) or through the EDI (Échange de Données Informatisé) system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending on December 31, the return must be filed by the second business day of May 1 (typically May 3). For other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of the year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, SIREN, address, legal form)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide French tax representative details if non-resident without permanent establishment
Report only French-source income attributable to a French permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions (e.g., tax credits, carryforward losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty benefits and foreign tax credits as applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculation (IS) and surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply reduced rate for eligible SMEs; ensure no double taxation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay (capped at 10% additional), and a 5% penalty for failure to file. Interest on late payments at 0.20% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard rate for non-residents, subject to tax treaty reduction)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident must provide a tax residency certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and submit a request via Form 5000 (for dividends) or Form 5001 (for interest/royalties) to the French tax authority. The reduced rate is applied at source if the forms are submitted before payment; otherwise, a refund claim can be made.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33.33%, reduced to 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions are met (e.g., 25% shareholding, effective substance). Interest: statutory rate 30%, reduced under tax treaties (typically 0-15%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million (turnover or total assets) for full documentation (Master File and Local File); simplified documentation for entities with turnover or assets between €50 million and €400 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies OECD BEPS principles and has a general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) under Article L.64 of the Tax Procedure Code. While no specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) exist, substance is required to avoid challenges to the corporate veil and to benefit from tax treaties or EU directives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code). Civil penalties: 40% to 80% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed fraud or serious misconduct. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without economic substance, lacking real business activity, or serving as a conduit for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 40% penalty for abuse of law (Article L.64).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for the company's tax debts if the corporate veil is pierced due to artificiality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures, suspicious transaction reporting, or due diligence for high-risk clients
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 10% of turnover for legal entities (Monetary and Financial Code). Criminal penalties for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned up to 5 years for money laundering offenses (Article 324-1 of the Penal Code).
